explanation: The pole fires on the grammatical 'glue' of running text rather than on its referents: short closed-class function words (prepositions of/with/for/from/in/by, articles the/a, subordinators where/while/when/which, quantifiers each/every/many), lexical verbs and the word-final fragments that complete them (ing, ed, ates, ulate), numerals and the glue punctuation of code ('(' opening a call or parameter list, '()>', ' {', '@param'), while it stays near zero on nouns, proper names, adjectives, copulas and auxiliaries (is/was/are/be/have), coordinators (and/or), pronouns (it/this) and clause punctuation (',' '.'). Its largest peaks (~1.5-1.9 of the 1.86 maximum) additionally need the glue token to be the expected continuation of the word just before it - 'of' after a spatial part or relational noun (side, front, top, corner, middle, edge, part, name), 'with' after a concrete/technical noun (document, thread, format, class, place, members), '(' after an identifier - and the same token in an abstract or formal frame ('list of', 'presence of', 'patient with', 'keys on') stays near zero, with code or forum context adding a further 1.5-2x.
